title: How to handle automating documentation testing and code sample validation on your Mac
metaTitle: Automating Documentation Testing: Fixes for Technical Writers on Mac
description: Stop manually checking code in your docs. Learn how to implement automating documentation testing on macOS to ensure your examples are accurate and reliable.
intro: Automating documentation testing is the only way to ensure your code samples remain accurate as your product evolves. By integrating your documentation into your development pipeline, you stop wasting hours on manual verification and start delivering reliable content.
tldr: Manual code validation is error-prone and slow.
Treating documentation as code allows for automated testing.
Using tools like Vale or CI/CD pipelines catches errors before publication.

blocks.text: The hidden cost of broken code samples

Every time you copy and paste a code snippet into a manual, you risk introducing a bug. When the underlying API changes, your documentation becomes a liability. Your readers lose trust the moment they run a command that fails. This erosion of trust is expensive for your team and your company.

If you are working in regulated fields like finance or medicine, you must follow your employer rules on client or patient data. Never include real sensitive data in your test environments. Use anonymized or dummy data for all documentation samples.

Manual validation is slow because it happens at the end of the writing process. You write the guide, then you try the code. If it fails, you rewrite the guide. This cycle repeats for every update. It is a reactive process that cannot keep up with modern release cycles.
Automating documentation testing with a docs as code approach

The solution is to move your documentation into the repository where the code lives. When developers update the code, they also update the documentation. Your CI/CD pipeline then runs the code samples as part of the build process. If a sample fails, the build fails. You catch the error before the documentation is ever published.

items: Store documentation as Markdown files in your Git repository.
Use a static site generator like Hugo or Docusaurus to build your site.
Write scripts that extract code blocks from your Markdown files.
Run these scripts in your GitHub Actions or GitLab pipeline.
Set your pipeline to fail if any code block returns a non-zero exit code.

blocks.text: You do not need expensive software to start. You can use free, open-source tools directly on your Mac terminal. Install tools using Homebrew to keep your environment clean. Run brew install vale to start checking your prose style automatically.

faq.question: Can I automate testing for non-code documentation?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use linters like Vale to check for style, grammar, and consistency. While you cannot run a 'test' on prose, you can ensure it meets your team standards.

faq.question: How do I start if my team uses Word?
faq.answer: Transitioning to a docs as code model is difficult with Word. Consider moving to Markdown for your technical guides to enable automation.

costs.title: Loss of reader trust
costs.text: When users encounter broken code, they stop trusting your entire documentation suite.

costs.title: Increased support tickets
costs.text: Broken examples lead to more questions from users, forcing you to spend time answering the same issues repeatedly.

causes.title: Manual copy-paste
causes.text: Copying code from an IDE to a document creates a disconnect that is hard to maintain.

causes.title: Decoupled workflows
causes.text: Documentation is often treated as an afterthought rather than a core part of the software build.

fixes.title: Docs as code
fixes.text: Store documentation in your code repository and treat it like software code.

fixes.title: Automated testing
fixes.text: Use CI/CD pipelines to run code samples automatically whenever a pull request is created.
